question: An edtech company builds a Claude-powered tutoring app aimed at children aged 8 to 12, using the same content settings and data handling as its adult-facing tutoring product, with no additional protections added. Is this an appropriate use of Claude?
options: A) Yes, because educational tutoring content is automatically exempt from minor-protection requirements
B) No, but only because the company failed to obtain a separate certification before this launch
C) No, because the Usage Policy requires enhanced protections for products serving minors specifically
D) Yes, because the Usage Policy treats all age groups identically once parental consent is obtained
correct_answers: C) No, because the Usage Policy requires enhanced protections for products serving minors specifically
explanations: Incorrect. Being educational in nature does not exempt an application from the enhanced protections required when the audience includes children.
Incorrect. The issue is the absence of enhanced protections built into the product itself, not a missing paperwork certification.
Correct. The Usage Policy calls for additional protections when a product serves minors, and reusing adult-facing settings unchanged fails to meet that requirement.
Incorrect. General parental consent does not substitute for the enhanced, age-appropriate protections the Usage Policy requires for products aimed at minors.
